clue.text: One making good case for a beer is helpful after losing the back 9

definitions.text: One making good case for a beer

indicators.note: losing says a run of letters is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: helpful means willing to work with others, cooperative

indicators.note: the back means the referenced entry is read from its back end to its front

parts.note: 9 refers to the answer at 9-across, the musical EVITA

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who keeps the beer barrels in good repair, with a puzzling bit about losing the back nine of a golf round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The back 9' reads 9-across, EVITA, backwards as ATIVE; 'losing' removes ATIVE from COOPERATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooper is a craftsman who makes and repairs casks, the wooden containers that hold beer.

clue.text: Revolutionary Polish setter's "little angels"

parts.note: Che Guevara was a Marxist revolutionary
to polish is to rub
setter's is short for setter is, I'm

explanation.surface: A revolutionary Pole's cherubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubim are winged child-like angels in art, the plural of cherub.

clue.text: Some of those flying in to Rio less

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the next words

explanation.surface: Fewer passengers flying into Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: Orioles are a family of songbirds, some of the creatures that fly.

clue.text: Fair point, fairly short and clever

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: fairly in the sense of rather, quite
clever means capable, able

explanation.surface: A judge of a contest calls something fair, fairly brief and clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable treatment is just and impartial, a synonym of fair.

clue.text: Schubert's "Unfinished" ultimately ends in octaves

parts.note: Schubert's Unfinished Symphony is his Symphony No 8, his eighth

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Schubert's Unfinished Symphony ending in octaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave spans eight notes, and in music the interval is also called an eighth.

clue.text: Perhaps drove someone else's vehicle once?

definitions.text: Perhaps drove someone else's vehicle once?

parts.words: Perhaps drove someone else's vehicle once?
parts.note: a second-hand car was once driven by its previous owner

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone borrowed a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-hand automobile is one another owner drove before.

clue.text: Having a key to one's heart? Beer, mostly

indicators.note: heart takes the central letter of one
mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Beer as the key to someone's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of 'one' is N; 'mostly' trims ALE to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Music based on a key centre is described as tonal.

clue.text: Subject boy or girl revised, without any resistance

indicators.note: revised means the letters are reworked into a new order
without any means every instance of the letter is taken out

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance, here both occurrences

explanation.surface: A subject a boy or girl revises without resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without any' removes both Rs from BOYORGIRL, leaving BOYOGIL to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of living things is a school subject.

clue.text: Leeds game? Time for one with most minutes under his belt

definitions.text: one with most minutes under his belt

indicators.note: game suggests the letters are ready to play and move around

explanation.surface: A Leeds football match and the player with the most minutes on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minutes under his belt' sounds like football, but it means the most time lived.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest sibling has lived longest, idiomatically having the most time under the belt.

clue.text: Anonymous female with no unreturnable serve

parts.note: an ace is a serve the opponent cannot return
less as a suffix means with no

explanation.surface: An unknown woman tennis player without a single ace.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a known identity, someone without a face in public is anonymous.

clue.text: Female having sex in musical

indicators.note: having means the name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name
IT is a common crossword term for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: A woman has a love scene in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lloyd Webber and Rice show about Eva Perón, so an example of a musical.

clue.text: New club for former England manager

parts.note: new in the sense of inexperienced, green
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A football association picks a fresh club for an old national coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Ron Greenwood managed the England football team from 1977 to 1982.

clue.text: Bad guts after eating pork pie that's nasty in the extreme

indicators.note: eating means the scrambled letters swallow the other piece
bad suggests the letters of the word are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie

explanation.surface: Stomach trouble after a pork pie, the nastiest feeling of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts the fib inside UGST, which 'Bad' makes of the guts. Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it, so a pork pie is a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly means nasty or unpleasant, so its superlative is the extreme of nastiness.

clue.text: Operatic soprano reportedly hard as nails

indicators.note: reportedly says we take the name as it is heard, not as it is written

parts.note: Maria Callas was a celebrated opera soprano

explanation.surface: A famous opera diva is said to be ruthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfeeling and unmoved by others' suffering is idiomatically hard as nails.

clue.text: Put out dips and sauces, each on a regular basis

indicators.note: each on a regular basis takes every other letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying out dips and sauces at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'dips' give IS; alternate letters of 'sauces' give SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to release or publish it, to put it out.

clue.text: Cider that's delicious, if for one Mike Pence

indicators.note: for one means one letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: scrummy is British slang for delicious
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cider described as delicious, with a nod to the former US vice-president Mike Pence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike Pence' looks like the politician but gives M and P: P replaces one M in SCRUMMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is a rough, strong farmhouse cider from the West of England.

clue.text: Potential life-saver when 1A 30 is short of oxygen and lacks energy

indicators.note: lacks means the following letter goes
is short of says those letters are missing

parts.note: 1A 30 refers to the linked answer at 1-across and 30-across
oxygen is O2, two Os
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cask-maker lacking air and energy needs a life-saver.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxygen as a molecule is O2, so both Os leave; then E goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation is first aid that can save a life.

clue.text: Second impassioned (but not explosive) part of a symphony?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: but not says the letters for the explosive are removed

parts.note: impassioned means vehement
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: An impassioned yet restrained second section of a symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is divided into self-contained sections called movements.

clue.text: Source of tension? New rosters introduced by 18D

indicators.note: introduced by says the abbreviation leads in

parts.note: the answer at 18-down is a club, abbreviated S for society

indicators.note: new means the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: New rotas imposed by a club as a cause of tension.
explanation.definitionFit: A stressor is anything that causes stress or strain.

clue.text: Religious types? There are 7 of them in London

definitions.text: There are 7 of them in London
definitions.meaning: Seven ... is a district of north London

explanation.surface: A question about nuns, then a riddle about a London place.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a female religious order are called sisters, and Seven Sisters is a London area and Tube station.

clue.text: Club sandwich on ciabatta is easily toasted? Yes, for starters

indicators.note: for starters takes the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A club sandwich on ciabatta toasts easily, yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club sandwich' wants to be one phrase; 'Club' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A society is an association of members, like a club.

clue.text: Pledge made by composer in Estonia …

indicators.note: in puts the composer within the country

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A pledge made by a composer in Estonia.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest money is a deposit paid as a pledge of good faith.

clue.text: … for there to be more composed, one of two playing 18A heard

indicators.note: heard says the name is taken as spoken

parts.note: Serena Williams is one of two tennis-playing sisters

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, a composer calmer when one of the Williams sisters plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means calm and composed, so the comparative is calmer.

clue.text: Call going against first of 18A in the second set finally

parts.note: V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the numeral

parts.note: the second is two, II in Roman numerals

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the referenced answer

parts.note: 18A refers to the answer at 18-across

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tennis line call goes against one of the Williams sisters as the second set ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to pay them a visit.

clue.text: Found one in leading role with sheep

parts.note: a star plays the leading role
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A sheep found in the starring role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like a past participle but is the verb to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a business is to set it up, start it up.

clue.text: Meals served topless in more than one part of Oxford?

definitions.text: more than one part of Oxford?

indicators.note: topless says the first letter is cut off

parts.note: suppers are evening meals

explanation.surface: Topless dinners in a corner of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a laced shoe, not just the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper is the top section of a shoe such as an Oxford.

clue.text: Bullfighter in ring right after photo taken by adult daughter

indicators.note: taken by says the photo comes first, followed by the next letters
after says the following letters come behind what precedes

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A bullfighter in the arena, photographed by a grown-up daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the mounted lancer in a bullfight who goads the bull.

clue.text: Religious beliefs that could make you go mad

indicators.note: that could make you says the letters of the phrase can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Religious doctrine that drives people crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down by a church as true.

clue.text: A politician in a fit of anger gets to rush around wildly

indicators.note: in places the pair inside the angry word

parts.note: a fit of anger is rage
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A furious MP charges about wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to run about violently and out of control.

clue.text: At any time, place for putting a tree?

parts.note: at any time means ever
a green is where golfers putt

explanation.surface: Asking where, at any time, a tree might be planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' suggests placing, but it is the golf stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine or holly keeps its leaves all year, so it is an example of an evergreen.

clue.text: Bum question a test includes

indicators.note: includes says the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A bottom question appearing in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Nates is the anatomical Latin word for the buttocks.

clue.text: Younger for one, in short series about my past being dodgy

indicators.note: about means the short word goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: ser is an abbreviation of series

indicators.note: being dodgy suggests the letters are shifty and out of order

explanation.surface: A spy chief with a dodgy past is the subject of a short series.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Alex Younger was head of MI6, Britain's foreign intelligence service.
explanation.definitionFit: As a former chief of the intelligence service, he is an example of a spy chief.
